title: Restore KV-cache runtime metrics and re-link tracing spans to Console incident views
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: During two urgent customer escalations (hosted + dedicated customers) we discovered that per-model KV-cache metrics (hits/misses/effective-cache-size) were missing from the Console and several dashboards showed stale or zeroed values. Additionally, distributed tracing links from the inference runtime to the Console incident pages were intermittently broken, which prevented on-call from diagnosing tail-latency spikes. This ticket tracks the investigation, root-cause remediation, and rollout for a fix that restores accurate KV-cache metrics and re-establishes trace linking across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Fix metric emission for KV-cache subsystem in the serving runtime and sidecars.
- Reconcile metric ingestion path (prometheus exporter -> metrics-ingest -> TSDB) and ensure dashboards reflect live values.
- Re-link trace IDs emitted by runtime to Console tracing UI (span attributes and trace-id propagation).
- Address config drift that caused the metric name/label change to be dropped during a recent refactor.

Impact:
- Affected customers experienced delayed incident resolution; several support tickets escalated to SEs.
- Observability gaps reduce our ability to enforce SLOs and validate rollout fallbacks (canary/A-B policy decisions).

Reproduction steps: (internal)
1) Deploy canary model and drive traffic with prefix-heavy prompts to exercise KV cache.
2) Query Console per-model dashboard and use metrics API (GET /api/metrics?model=<>) to confirm metrics missing.
3) Trigger a tail-latency load profile and confirm trace linkage broken by inspecting span tags in runtime logs.

Root cause hypothesis: During the runtime refactor in runtime-1.18 we renamed the metric labels from `kv_cache` -> `kvcache` to conform with new internal naming. The telemetry pipeline (metrics-emitter sidecar) was not updated in Dedicated/Private configs; the pipeline silently dropped the mismatched metrics at the ingest stage. Separately, a change to the tracing sidecar's header rewrite (to support new routing policy) stripped traceparent for some request paths, leading to missing spans in Console.

Proposed fix:
- Implement compatibility layer in metrics-emitter that emits both legacy `kv_cache_*` and new `kvcache_*` metric names for 4 weeks.
- Update ingest mapping rules in metrics-ingest service to accept both names and backfill recent TSDB buckets where possible.
- Patch tracing sidecar to preserve `traceparent` and `x-request-id` for inference requests; add automated integration test to catch header rewrite regressions.
- Add end-to-end smoke test in CI that validates a synthetic model emits KV cache metrics and that traces are visible in Console.

Rollout plan:
- Patch runtime + sidecars in staging, validate dashboards and traces for Hosted.
- Release to Dedicated as a non-breaking config update (customers will be notified) and offer an opt-in early upgrade for Private (with upgrade docs).
- Monitor metrics ingestion success rate and trace-linking heatmap for 72 hours post-deploy; automatic rollback if errors > 2% above baseline.

Success criteria:
- KV-cache metrics reappear in per-model dashboards and the metrics API within 30 minutes of deploy.
- Trace-linking restored end-to-end for 99.9% of sampling traffic for 72-hour window.
- No customer escalations remain open attributable to missing metrics/traces.

Follow-ups:
- Create an alert when ingestion pipeline drops > 0.1% of expected metric families.
- Document metric name-change policy and require cross-team config sync before renames.

Artifacts and links:
- Incident writeup (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/2025-02-kvcache-observability
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-models/kv-cache-health
- Repro harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-repro/tree/ENG-13245
- Initial PR for metrics-emitter compat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-emitter/pull/487
